title: The Absurd and the Revolt
text:
Albert Camus located the origin of philosophy in a single question: whether life is worth living. He called the confrontation between the human longing for meaning and a silent universe the absurd. Rather than surrendering to despair, Camus argued, the absurd man accepts this tension and continues to live with lucidity.

The response to the absurd, in Camus's view, is revolt rather than suicide or blind faith. Revolt means refusing to deny the contradiction while still choosing to act and to love fully. Sisyphus, condemned to push a stone endlessly up a hill, becomes for Camus a figure of quiet dignity.

questions.text: According to Camus, what is the origin of philosophy?
options: A question about whether life is worth living

questions.text: What does Camus describe as the absurd?
options: A confrontation between the human longing for meaning and a silent universe
A law of nature about gravity

questions.text: What does the passage suggest Camus rejects in response to the absurd?
Why is Sisyphus a figure of dignity for Camus?
options: Because he accepts an endless task while refusing despair
Because he finds a meaning that the universe provides
Because he stops pushing the stone

vocabulary.definition: the conflict between the human search for meaning and an indifferent universe
a refusal to submit to a situation one cannot accept
the quality of being worthy of respect

paragraph_translations: Albert Camus situou a origem da filosofia numa única pergunta: se a vida vale a pena ser vivida. Ele chamou de absurdo o confronto entre o anseio humano por sentido e um universo silencioso. Em vez de render-se ao desespero, argumentou Camus, o homem absurdo aceita essa tensão e continua a viver com lucidez.

A resposta ao absurdo, na visão de Camus, é a revolta, e não o suicídio nem a fé cega. Revoltar-se significa recusar-se a negar a contradição, ao mesmo tempo que se escolhe agir e amar plenamente. Sísifo, condenado a empurrar uma pedra morro acima para sempre, torna-se para Camus uma figura de dignidade silenciosa.
